flawed_step: Step 3: Inferring from single-vertex local optimality (each vertex has at least as many incident cut edges as uncut edges) that the partition is globally maximum is unjustified.
counterexample: Let G be the 4-cycle v1-v2-v3-v4-v1. For the partition {v1,v2}|{v3,v4}, the cut value is 2. Every vertex has one crossing and one noncrossing incident edge, so moving any single vertex leaves the cut value unchanged and cannot strictly improve it. However, {v1,v3}|{v2,v4} has cut value 4, so the original partition is not maximum.
assessment_summary: Single-vertex stability only establishes a local optimum under one-vertex moves, not a global maximum. The 4-cycle provides a direct counterexample.
